scope: pregnancy and clinical-form route guard controls
method: Read source only from immutable Git blobs using git show; exact-main git grep for dashboard callers; read-only independent security review; tests read but not run. No ClinicAI API/database/runtime/provider/VPS/production/secret/PHI access.
result: Extended SEC-010 with sibling /links metadata exposure under the same consent-router identity-only boundary; no new finding ID. Tenant invoice FK candidate deduplicates with DB-007; timeline direct-select candidate did not add a distinct permission scope versus the normal internal journey API; pregnancy and normal clinical form route checks did not yield a new candidate.

The checked-in production example uses a postgres database user; this is a template, not proof of the active secret value.
Service IO test returns relationship and form-code metadata; it does not exercise route role authorization and was not run.
Normal visit journey endpoints are available to internal staff; the table does not add a capability boundary absent from this API.

Operations diary is a separate ops.view route, scoped to identity.clinic_id.

Projection uses an event-specific field whitelist.

Consumer persists only the whitelist projection and deduplicates by event_id.
Projection has clinic-only SELECT RLS/grant. No new finding because the normal visit journey API already exposes the same projection to internal staff; runtime PostgREST was not tested.
Dashboard loads the normal API and uses table subscriptions to refresh; no direct PostgREST row-read was found in this component.
Company invoice references are separate FKs without a composite patient/company-clinic constraint.

Service validates the clinic-scoped patient before creating the company invoice.
Company selection is scoped to clinic and patient context.

Test rejects a company belonging to a different patient; read only, not run. Similar to DB-007, so no new finding.
Composite request-to-inventory transaction FK retains clinic and batch scope; staff FK is global.
Inventory request writer derives staff and clinic from identity; multi-clinic staff use is not shown to be a violation.
Full router read: medical read guard and service-owned write permission; no new issue in this slice.
Service checks pregnancy write capability rather than trusting the broad identity dependency.
Pregnancy reads require medical access and the patient is checked within identity clinic.
Create path checks writer permission, clinic-scoped patient and matching clinic-scoped visit.
Update path checks writer permission and scopes the pregnancy row by clinic.
Full router read: normal form read/write routes declare clinical capability guards; service-level coverage remains partial.

reviewed_candidates.rationale: The direct table grant is clinic-only, but the normal visit-journey API uses cua_noi_bo and returns the same event-specific whitelist to internal staff. Dashboard usage here is API fetch plus refresh subscription. No PostgREST request was run; ops.view diary is a separate route and not conflated with visit history.

Schema FKs are not composite-scoped to clinic/patient, but the service validates clinic and patient before write and the existing test rejects a different patient's company. This is a defense-in-depth gap, not a demonstrated current service path failure; retain under DB-007's broader relationship invariant.

The migration has a global staff FK, but the reviewed writer takes actor identity from the current staff and that staff may be active in multiple clinics. No cross-clinic write or identity mismatch was shown.

validation.application_tests: not run; relevant source tests read only

limitations: The /links exposure assumes the backend database role can read the rows under the application's DATABASE_URL; the checked-in production example uses postgres, but the active secret/runtime role was not inspected.
No dashboard string match was found for /links/ConsentService; dynamically constructed callers and API UUID discovery were not verified.
The timeline projection stores only event-specific whitelisted fields; the normal internal visit-journey route already returns that projection. No direct PostgREST request was run.
Company invoice schema lacks a composite patient/clinic FK, but reviewed service/test evidence does not show a current cross-tenant write; retained as a DB-007 defense-in-depth relationship pattern.
Test results were not executed. All conclusions are static and exact-main; no incident or real patient exposure is claimed.
